nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite search space, $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set, and $u$ the uniform amplitude vector, given by $u(x) = 1/\sqrt{|\alpha|}$ for every $x \in \alpha$. For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\psi_k$ be the vector obtained from $u$ by applying the Grover step for $M$ $k$ times. Then $\sum_{x \in \alpha} \psi_k(x)^2 = 1$.
nodes.title: Grover iterates of the uniform state are unit vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite search space and $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set. For every real amplitude vector $\psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\psi_k$ be the vector obtained from $\psi$ by applying the Grover step for $M$ $k$ times. Then $\sum_{x \in \alpha} \psi_k(x)^2 = \sum_{x \in \alpha} \psi(x)^2$.
nodes.title: Grover iteration preserves the squared norm

nodes.summary: For every nonempty finite type $\alpha$, the uniform amplitude vector on $\alpha$ has squared Euclidean norm $1$.
nodes.title: The uniform amplitude vector is normalized

nodes.summary: For a finite type $\alpha$ and a real amplitude vector $\psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, the squared norm of $\psi$ is its squared Euclidean norm $\sum_{x \in \alpha} \psi(x)^2$.
nodes.title: Squared norm of an amplitude vector

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ (the search space), a real amplitude vector indexed by $\alpha$ is a function $\psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, assigning a real amplitude to each point of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Real amplitude vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite search space and $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set with complement $M^c$. For a real number $\varphi$, this is the real amplitude vector on $\alpha$ whose value is $\sin\varphi / \sqrt{|M|}$ at every point of $M$ and $\cos\varphi / \sqrt{|M^c|}$ at every point of $M^c$.
nodes.title: Symmetric Grover state at a given angle

nodes.summary: For a finite type $\alpha$, the diffusion operator sends a real amplitude vector $\psi$ on $\alpha$ to the amplitude vector $x \mapsto 2\bar\psi - \psi(x)$, where $\bar\psi$ is the arithmetic mean of the amplitudes of $\psi$.
nodes.title: Inversion about the mean

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of marked elements of a finite search space of size $N$, and let $\theta = \arcsin \sqrt{|M| / N}$ be its Grover angle. The standard iteration count is $\lfloor \pi / (4\theta) \rfloor$, the largest natural number at most $\pi / (4\theta)$; it is $0$ when $\theta = 0$, that is, when no element is marked.
nodes.title: Standard Grover iteration count

nodes.summary: For a finite search space $\alpha$ and a marked set $M \subseteq \alpha$, the Grover angle of $M$ is $\theta = \arcsin \sqrt{|M| / |\alpha|}$, where the quotient $|M| / |\alpha|$ is taken to be $0$ when $\alpha$ is empty.
nodes.title: Grover angle

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite search space and $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a real amplitude vector $\psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, the $k$-th Grover iterate of $\psi$ is the vector obtained by applying the Grover step for $M$ to $\psi$ $k$ times; the $0$-th iterate is $\psi$ itself.
nodes.title: Grover iterate

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite search space, $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set and $\theta$ the Grover angle of $M$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the Grover phase of $M$ after $k$ iterations is the real number $(2k + 1)\theta$.
nodes.title: Grover phase

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and $M \subseteq \alpha$ a set of marked elements. Write $O_M$ for the phase oracle, which negates the amplitudes at the points of $M$, and $D$ for inversion about the mean, which sends an amplitude vector $\varphi$ on $\alpha$ to $x \mapsto 2\bar\varphi - \varphi(x)$, where $\bar\varphi$ is the arithmetic mean of the amplitudes of $\varphi$. One Grover step sends a real amplitude…
nodes.title: Grover step

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of marked elements of a finite search space of size $N$, let $M^c$ be the set of unmarked elements, and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. With $\mu = (|M^c|\, b - |M|\, a) / N$, the next marked amplitude is $2\mu + a$.
nodes.title: Marked amplitude after a Grover step

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite search space and $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set such that both $M$ and its complement are nonempty, and let $\theta = \arcsin \sqrt{|M| / |\alpha|}$ be the Grover angle of $M$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\psi_k$ be the vector obtained by applying the Grover step for $M$ $k$ times to the uniform amplitude vector, whose value is $1/\sqrt{|\alpha|}$ at every point. Then the marked…
nodes.title: Exact success probability of Grover search

nodes.summary: For a real amplitude vector $\psi$ on a type $\alpha$ and a finite set $M \subseteq \alpha$ of marked elements, the marked probability is $\sum_{x \in M} \psi(x)^2$. When $\alpha$ is finite and $\psi$ has squared norm $1$, this is the probability of observing a marked outcome.
nodes.title: Probability of the marked outcomes

nodes.summary: For a finite type $\alpha$ and a real amplitude vector $\psi$ on $\alpha$, the mean amplitude of $\psi$ is $\bigl(\sum_{x \in \alpha} \psi(x)\bigr) / |\alpha|$, the arithmetic mean of its amplitudes. When $\alpha$ is empty it is $0$.
nodes.title: Mean amplitude

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a nonempty set of marked elements of a finite search space of size $N$ with $4|M| = N$. Starting from the uniform amplitude vector, one Grover iteration produces an amplitude vector whose marked probability is $1$.
nodes.title: One Grover iteration suffices when a quarter is marked

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of marked elements of a finite search space of size $N$, let $M^c$ be the set of unmarked elements, and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. The oracle mean is $(|M^c|\, b - |M|\, a) / N$.
nodes.title: Mean amplitude after the phase oracle

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ and a finite set $M \subseteq \alpha$ of marked elements, the phase oracle sends a real amplitude vector $\psi$ on $\alpha$ to the amplitude vector whose value at $x$ is $-\psi(x)$ if $x \in M$ and $\psi(x)$ if $x \notin M$; that is, it negates exactly the amplitudes at the marked elements.
nodes.title: Phase oracle

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of marked elements of a search space $\alpha$, and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. The symmetric amplitude vector with marked amplitude $a$ and unmarked amplitude $b$ is the real amplitude vector on $\alpha$ whose value is $a$ at every element of $M$ and $b$ at every element outside $M$.
nodes.title: Symmetric amplitude vector

nodes.summary: For a finite type $\alpha$, the uniform amplitude vector on $\alpha$ is the real amplitude vector whose value at every point is $1/\sqrt{|\alpha|}$, where $|\alpha|$ is the number of elements of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Uniform amplitude vector

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of marked elements of a finite search space of size $N$, let $M^c$ be the set of unmarked elements, and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. With $\mu = (|M^c|\, b - |M|\, a) / N$, the next unmarked amplitude is $2\mu - b$.
nodes.title: Unmarked amplitude after a Grover step

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
